name: NeuroForecast split-optimism study
status: Written and hashed before any run of the study code. Development data only: both sealed tests are spent.
question: How much do weaker validation designs overstate the accuracy and interval coverage of day-7 to day-12 forecasts on neuronal MEA assays, compared with the design a lab meets in use (a new culture batch testing new chemicals)? Do they change which model looks best?
disclosure: A feasibility probe on 2026-10-08 used one model (Extra Trees with max_features 0.5 and min_samples_leaf 2 on the same 13 inputs), one fold assignment per design, and intervals from a random calibration quarter. Its date-macro MAE was 0.590 (random condition), 0.599 (chemical held out), 0.669 (batch held out) and 0.706 (batch and chemical held out); pooled coverage at nominal 0.80 was 0.80, 0.79, 0.74 and 0.735. The hypotheses below were written after seeing that probe.

All 41 batches were already used by the locked v3 model study (2026-10-07), so batch_chemical performance is known for the v2 recipe (0.690 on the v3 folds) and for LightGBM and ridge on other feature sets.
This protocol is self-attested unless its SHA-256 appears in a public commit before the study's results do.

data.inputs: the 13 columns of SMALL_COLUMNS in tools/neuroforecast_harness.py (activity and coordination readouts at days 5 and 7 relative to same-plate controls, and log concentration); nothing after day 7
data.target: day-12 log2 replicate-mean network spikes relative to the same-plate day-12 control median (the target of both sealed tests)

designs.random_condition: conditions assigned to folds at random; culture batches and chemicals are shared between training and test
designs.chemical: chemicals held out; the test chemicals' culture batches also appear in training
designs.batch: culture batches held out; the test chemicals may appear in training on other batches
designs.batch_chemical: culture batches held out and every chemical tested on them purged from training (the design of both sealed tests and the v3 study)

folds.assignment: tools/neuroforecast_harness.fold_assignment with repetition r = 0..4: a seeded random permutation of conditions, chemicals or batches, dealt round-robin into folds. Inner folds apply the same design inside each outer training set (neuroforecast_harness.inner_splits).

models.calibrated_day7: isotonic regression of day 12 on day 7 alone
models.ridge: ridge regression (alpha 30) on standardised inputs with median imputation; target is day 12 minus day 7
models.lightgbm: LightGBM with the v3 study's parameters (400 trees, learning rate 0.03, 15 leaves, min_child_samples 20, subsample 0.8 every iteration, colsample_bytree 0.8, reg_lambda 1, L1 objective), median imputation; target is day 12 minus day 7
models.extra_trees_v2: the shipped v2 recipe: Extra Trees with 256 trees, max_depth 12, min_samples_leaf 4, max_features 1.0, median imputation; target is day 12 directly

fitting: Every model is fit on the usable training conditions only, with random_state 20261008. Outer test predictions come from the model refit on the whole outer training set.
intervals: Constant-width split-conformal intervals per outer fold, at levels 0.80 and 0.90: half-width is the ceil((n+1) level)-th smallest absolute inner out-of-fold residual of the same model under the same design.

metrics.date_macro_mae: absolute error averaged over doses within a chemical, then over chemicals within a batch, then equally over batches; per batch, losses are averaged over the 5 repetitions
metrics.apparent_coverage: each design's own intervals on its own outer test folds: pooled, batch mean, and the worst fifth of batches (mean of the lowest 8 of 41 batch coverages), averaged over repetitions
metrics.transfer_coverage: an interval half-width validated under design X (the conformal quantile of all of that model's outer out-of-fold absolute residuals under X, same repetition) applied to the same model's batch_chemical outer out-of-fold residuals: pooled and worst fifth, averaged over repetitions
metrics.ranking: models ordered by date-macro MAE under each design; Kendall tau of each design's order against batch_chemical; the best model under each design

inference: Design comparison: batch-paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 20261008) of the per-batch loss difference between design X and batch_chemical for the same model, after averaging over repetitions.

hypotheses.H1_primary: For extra_trees_v2, the chemical design's date-macro MAE is at least 5% below batch_chemical's (optimism >= 0.05), and the paired 95% interval of the difference lies wholly below zero.
hypotheses.H2: The same holds for the random_condition design.
hypotheses.H3: For extra_trees_v2 at nominal 0.80, transfer coverage from the chemical design and from the random_condition design, each measured on batch_chemical residuals, is at most 0.77.
hypotheses.H4_descriptive: Optimism for every learned model; whether holding out batches alone recovers most of the gap (batch shift against chemical novelty); apparent worst-fifth coverage by design; ranking agreement and the best model per design.

outputs.release: evaluation/harness/split_study/: per-case out-of-fold predictions and interval half-widths for every design, repetition and model (oof.csv.gz), the summary (summary.json) and the lock (lock.json)

lock: tools/neuroforecast_split_study.py records the SHA-256 of this protocol, of itself and of tools/neuroforecast_harness.py before its first run, and refuses to run if any of them changes afterwards. The analysis is recomputed from oof.csv.gz alone.
